Subject: Holdback + tranche release approach for renewal & mid-contract capacity increase

Hi Sara / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the detailed usage notes — the Q1 report helped a lot. Per our call, I wanted to propose a simple structure that lets Lumina add mid-cycle capacity now while preserving renewal alignment and minimizing billing shock. High level:

- Holdback credit: Redwood invoices the uplift in two tranches. 70% invoiced at amendment signature; 30% held back and released after the first 90 days of increased usage if cumulative consumption meets the agreed threshold.
- Prorated invoice slices: We’ll pro-rate the 70% tranche to the remainder of your term so you don’t pay a full year up front.
- Conditional discount tiers: If weekly average token usage in months 1–3 is >120% of baseline, Lumina qualifies for an additional 5% refund applied to the held-back tranche.

This approach keeps the renewal co-term intact and gives you runway to ramp without an immediate large uplift. I attached an initial amendment stub and a short Q1 usage CSV for transparency.

Questions for Procurement/Finance:
- Is a 90-day release window workable for your PO/payment cadence?
- Any constraints from your revenue/expense forecast side on splitting invoices this way?

I’m looping in our pricing lead (karthik) and finance (naomi) to confirm revenue recognition and discount impacts. If this looks directionally acceptable we can produce an executable amendment and DocuSign link.

Best,
Tessa
Account Lead | Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Lumina’s procurement questions. Need quick alignment so we can get the amendment to them before their CFO review next week. TL;DR: they asked about net-45 payment, baseline definition, and an audit clause.

Options I see:
A) Commercial-first: accept net-45, define baseline as Q1 monthly average tokens (simple), allow a single light audit with 30 days notice. Keeps sale moving but slightly delays cash.
B) Revenue-protected: push for net-30 on the initial tranche or require a short prepaid buffer equal to 15% of the tranche to protect cash/recognition. Baseline can be Q1 but we add a reconciliation clause to settle differences at renewal.

Kar, can you confirm the delta to unit economics for option A vs B (approx % discount/credit impact)? Naomi, what’s the impact on revenue recognition and any finance approvals needed? Marissa, any legal redlines we should expect on audit language?

Goal: turn this into a short amendment (1–2 pages) with clear measurement terms and a DocuSign link.

Thanks — Tessa

Quick calc on the two options (high level):

- Option A (accept net-45, 90-day release): incremental risk to Redwood ~ 2.2% of uplift dollar value due to extended payment window + potential refund exposure under the 5% performance refund. Economically we can absorb this within current discount bands; margin impact is modest.

- Option B (require net-30 or a 15% short prepaid buffer): reduces cash and refund exposure to <0.5% but will introduce friction for Lumina procurement.

Recommendation: Offer Option A as the default and include Option B as an escalated pathway if Lumina requests accelerated uplift or >2x baseline immediate usage. For the CFO cover note — suggest this language: "Redwood will record the uplift as deferred revenue for the portion invoiced but subject to holdback; held funds will be recognized upon verification of usage thresholds or returned per amendment terms." Naomi — please refine for GAAP/ASC if needed.
